coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Edwin M. Lee Apartments (Block 3 East)
record.summary: Edwin M. Lee Apartments, an affordable multifamily building at 1150 Third Street on Mission Bay South Block 3 East: a five-story building with offices, a garage and a community room, sponsored by the Chinatown Community Development Center with Swords to Plowshares. The city permit was filed in December 2016 and marked complete on June 17, 2020; the Examiner reported that it had housed residents since February (2021) and that the grand opening was held in May 2021. Sources disagree on the unit count (119 or 118).

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- an idealized rectangle (constructed by Pier & Point: it shares Venue's real east edge and orientation, widened to the real 3rd St curb line), not a hand trace or surveyed footprint. The building it stands for is identified by DataSF's address point for 1150 3rd St (inside the polygon) and by parcel 8711026, which overlaps 93% of the polygon (99% of the parcel); no source read gives the building's own footprint.
notes.digitized_from: A construction by Pier & Point, not a hand trace: the east edge of Venue's outline as fitted to a rectangle (72.07m, the edge facing 3rd St), extended east as a rectangle of the same length and orientation and widened until it reaches the 3rd St curb line as estimated from DataSF's official street centerlines (half-width 6.8m).

facts.value: 8711 / 026 (per the DataSF permit records); Venue, 1155 4th St, is on the same block, lot 025
Chinatown Community Development Center with Swords to Plowshares (project sponsor per OCII fiscal year 2015-16 report)
Leddy Maytum Stacy Architects (with Saida + Sullivan Design Partners), per SF YIMBY; OCII's report spells the firm "Stacey"

The sources disagree and this record does not pick one: 119 units per OCII's fiscal year 2015-16 report and the permit; 118 per the Examiner (May 2021) and the Chinatown Community Development Center page ('62 units designated for formerly homeless veterans and 56 units for low-income families').
$78 million from federal, state and city sources, per SF YIMBY (a news report)

DataSF's official address point for 1150 3rd St (address ID 741013, parcel 8711026) lies inside this record's outline, 8.4 m from its nearest edge. Parcel 8711026 overlaps 93% of the outline, and the outline covers 99% of the parcel. The overlap and distance are Pier & Point's own calculation in a local metric projection; the outline itself is still an approximate rectangle, not a surveyed footprint.

open_questions: Does the outline match the building's real footprint? The address point and the parcel fit it, but no source read gives the footprint, so the shape remains an approximation.

Unit count differs between sources: 119 (OCII report, permit, SFBay 2018 plan), 118 (Chinatown Community Development Center page, SF YIMBY, Examiner), and 62 veteran plus 57 family units per Swords to Plowshares against 62 plus 56 elsewhere. The sources do not reconcile these (the extra unit may be a manager's unit; that is not stated in any source read).
Square footage differs: SF YIMBY gives 123,700 and the Chinatown Community Development Center page gives 81,295; not reconciled, so neither is recorded as a fact.

The exact move-in date is not stated: the Examiner (May 2021) says residents since 'February' without naming the year, and the permit shows completion in June 2020. The 2020-06-17 milestone is the permit's own completion date, not an occupancy date.
No OCII Commission document or press release for the opening was read as text; the primary-source figures come from OCII's fiscal year 2015-16 report and the city permit data.
Final construction cost was not found; the $73,040,010 is a 2016 projection and the $45,000,000 is the permit's own estimate.
